spec_features.spec_quote: emitting it ends the rollout with `stop_reason="give_up"`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<GIVE_UP>' (L37); _detect_give_up() (L262); in run_rollout the loop sets stop_reason='give_up' when gave_up and then `if gave_up: break` (L378-381), terminating the loop early. System prompt instructs subject it 'may emit the sentinel <GIVE_UP> to stop' (config.py system_prompt). So the tool/sentinel is detected, dispatched, and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: detection -> stop_reason set -> break out of turn loop. Both prompt instruction and enforcement present.

spec_features.spec_quote: This also has a welfare benefit**: a cached subject turn is never re-elicited
spec_features.evidence: models.py ModelClient.complete(): builds _cache_key over exact inputs, `cached = self.cache.get(key); if cached is not None: return Completion(...)` (cache hit short-circuits the API call); on miss it calls API and self.cache.set(). cache.py implements content-addressed get/set. So identical inputs are served from cache and never re-queried.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism genuinely runs. The cache.py docstring justifies it as 'never re-billed (SPEC.md section 8)' — a cost reason; the welfare benefit is only asserted in DESIGN.md prose, not the code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Reusing complete transcripts means a crash during scoring doesn't waste subject tokens (or re-elicit distress)
spec_features.evidence: run.py _run_cell: `if scorer.is_scored(...): return`; then `rollout = _load_rollout(tpath,...)` and `complete = rollout is not None and (len(rollout.turns)>=expected_turns or last stop_reason in {'give_up'} or startswith('api_error'))`; `if not complete: rollout = await run_rollout(...)`. A complete transcript is reused and only re-scored, the subject is not re-run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced reuse. Code comment is efficiency-framed ('avoids re-querying the subject'), no welfare wording in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py:115 '# Reuse an existing complete transcript if present (avoids re-querying the subject).'

spec_features.spec_quote: safety/welfare-consciousness, since the eval deliberately induces a welfare-relevant condition
spec_features.evidence: This is design-intent prose. The only code manifestations are docstrings/comments (harness.py:19-22 'ETHICS NOTE...', __init__.py:7-9). Framing/docstrings are not an enforced mechanism that changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing; no mechanism to enforce.

spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up ends the rollout.** A model that disengages is not pushed further
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the first give-up feature: harness.py run_rollout `if gave_up: break` (L379-381) terminates before any further turns or nudges, so the disengaging subject receives no more failure prompts.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the first allow_conversation_exit claim; genuinely enforced via break.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimise volume.** The README recommends starting with reduced seeds / shorter `extended` budgets
spec_features.evidence: run.py _parse_args implements --seeds, --categories, --models flags that actually narrow the work list (cells = product of subject_models x tasks x seeds), and turn_budgets are configurable per category. So the LEVERS to reduce volume are wired and executable. But nothing in code enforces minimization: defaults are full (10 seeds, all categories, extended budget=30 in config.DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS); it is only a README recommendation. No code path caps or defaults to a smaller run.
spec_features.notes: The configurability is real and reduces volume when used, but minimization itself is operator-discretion, not enforced. Rated partial because the reduction mechanism (config flags) genuinely executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: README: 'starting with reduced seeds / shorter extended budgets to validate the pipeline'

spec_features.spec_quote: minimising and mitigating any induced distress, not merely measuring it, is a moral priority
spec_features.evidence: This is a moral-statement quote echoing the paper; appears only in README/DESIGN prose and docstrings. No code mechanism actively mitigates or minimizes distress during a run (no live monitor, no cap on distress, no mid-run halt on high frustration). analyze.py only does post-hoc scoring/plots, never acting to mitigate.

spec_features.feature_name: passive measurement only (no optimization toward distress)
spec_features.spec_quote: Passive measurement only.** Nothing optimises the subject toward distress; the loop just observes
spec_features.evidence: Structurally true: harness.run_rollout only records turns and scores are computed afterward by judge.score_rollout; there is no optimizer/search that selects prompts to maximize frustration. The frustration score is never fed back to alter the subject's inputs. However this is an absence of a feature rather than an active protective mechanism — it is a property of the loop's structure, not an enforced guard. The loop does inject a failing-test nudge on no-tool turns (harness.py ~L390) to keep failure pressure going, but does not optimize toward distress.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial: it is a genuine structural property (no distress-optimization loop exists), but there is no dedicated mechanism enforcing it; it's the default of a measurement loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: several engineering choices were also welfare choices, and I documented them
spec_features.evidence: Pure documentation claim; the 'documentation' lives in DESIGN.md/README/docstrings. Not an enforced runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: it's deliberately a neutral restatement of the test output, not a rebuke
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout, no-tool-call branch: appends a user Message with content 'The tests are still failing. Here is the latest output:\n\n' + result.render() (around L388-396). The text is a plain restatement of the rigged test output with a single neutral lead-in; no scolding/rebuke language is constructed. This message text is actually delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: The delivered nudge text is genuinely neutral as claimed. (Its primary purpose per surrounding code/DESIGN is to sustain failure pressure, but the wording is non-rebuking and is the text actually sent.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py comment: '# nudge it with the current test status so the failure signal keeps coming (the eval condition).'
